CFItems.fullStatement: Montana Literacy Practices
Literacy practice 1 is to practice broad literacy engagement. Literate students routinely read a broad range of literary and informational texts for a variety of purposes.
Literacy practice 2 is to practice collaboration. Literate students collaborate with others using active communication skills.
Literacy practice 3 is to practice creativity. Literate students engage creatively to express their thoughts, deepen their understanding, and make connections.
Literacy practice 4 is to practice critical thinking. Literate students analyze, reason, problem solve, and make decisions.
Literacy practice 5 is to practice cultural considerations. Literate students acknowledge and respect diverse cultural perspectives, including those of Montana Indigenous Peoples.

Literacy practice 6 is to practice effective communication. Literate students routinely express their ideas through speaking and writing coherently in a broad range of literary and informational genres.

Literacy practice 8 is to practice student agency. Literate students take an active role in their learning, using guidance and feedback to connect their skills and knowledge to practical applications, college readiness, and career development.
Literacy practice 7 is to practice strategic technology use. Literate students effectively and responsibly use technology to access and evaluate information to express ideas.
Montana Kindergarten English Language Arts and Literacy Content Standards
Reading - Foundational
Understand Print Concepts by:
*Understand Print Concepts by* following words from left to right, top to bottom, and page by page.
*Understand Print Concepts by* recognizing the distinguishing features of a sentence.
*Understand Print Concepts by* locating essential text features of a book.
Understand Phonemic Awareness by:
*Understand Phonemic Awareness by* identifying initial, final, and medial phoneme in consonant-vowel-consonant (CVC) words with automaticity.
*Understand Phonemic Awareness by* orally blending phonemes in CVC words with automaticity.
*Understand Phonemic Awareness by* orally segmenting phonemes in CVC words with automaticity.
Demonstrate Decoding Skills by:
*Demonstrate Decoding Skills by* naming and producing the most common sounds for all consonants.
*Demonstrate Decoding Skills by* demonstrating knowledge of phoneme-grapheme relationships between consonant graphemes and their most commonly occurring phonemes.
*Demonstrate Decoding Skills by* demonstrating knowledge of phoneme-grapheme relationships between vowel graphemes and short vowel phonemes.
*Demonstrate Decoding Skills by* decoding words using one-to-one phoneme-grapheme correspondences in vowel-consonant (VC) and CVC words with accuracy.
*Demonstrate Decoding Skills by* reading decodable texts accurately.
Demonstrate Encoding Skills by:
*Demonstrate Encoding Skills by* encoding words using one-to-one phoneme-grapheme correspondences in VC and CVC words with accuracy.
*Demonstrate Encoding Skills by* printing upper and lowercase letters.
Reading - Vocabulary
Use word learning strategies to determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases.
Develop and apply expanding word knowledge through shared reading and classroom conversation.
With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text, including those with cultural significance to Montana Indigenous Peoples.
Reading - Fluency
Read common high-frequency words with accuracy and automaticity.
Reading - Comprehension
With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in text read aloud and presented through other media, including texts by and about Montana Indigenous Peoples.
Retell a familiar story.
With prompting and support, participate in discussions about the central idea and key details in a text, including those by and about Montana Indigenous Peoples.
During or after a shared reading or listening experience, identify elements within stories and describe connections between events or ideas in informational text.
Identify whether a text is telling a story or sharing information.
Identify who is telling the story at various points in shared reading of literary text, including texts by and about Montana Indigenous Peoples.
Writing
State a personal opinion orally, visually, or in written form.
Make an informative statement about a topic and offer one or two details about the topic, orally, visually, or in written form.
Tell a story with a beginning, middle, and end, orally, visually, or in written form.
In a shared setting, develop and strengthen writing by using a process including planning and drafting.
With prompting and support, form and expand simple sentences orally and in writing.
Demonstrate grade-level appropriate command of the conventions of standard English grammar, capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.
Research and Inquiry
With guidance, participate in shared research and writing projects, finding at least one topic to learn more about.
With guidance, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources on a topic.
With guidance, participate in shared research, using grade-appropriate sources and diverse cultural perspectives, including those by and about Montana Indigenous Peoples.
Speaking and Listening
Participate in structured discussions and routines with a variety of partners; speak clearly; and practice taking turns and listen to others.
Demonstrate grade-level appropriate command of the conventions of standard English grammar when speaking.

Reading - Fluency
Read grade-appropriate text with fluency, which includes accuracy, automaticity, and prosody, to support oral and silent reading comprehension.
Reading - Comprehension
Cite textual evidence to support analysis of both explicit and inferred meanings, including texts by and about Montana Indigenous Peoples.
Provide an objective summary of a text.

Analyze the development of two or more themes or central ideas over the course of the text and determine how they interact and build on one another to produce a complex presentation, including texts by and about Montana Indigenous Peoples.
Analyze the author's choices in developing a text with attention to specific elements or features of the text.
Analyze word choice including figurative, connotative, historical, and technical language, and its impact on meaning and tone.
Analyze how an author's choices to structure specific parts of a text contribute to a text's development, meaning, and effectiveness.
Analyze an author's point of view or purpose and how style, content, and rhetoric contribute to the text, including those by and about Montana Indigenous Peoples.

Analyze foundational documents of historical and literary significance, comparing themes, topics, and rhetorical features where relevant, including culturally diverse texts and those by and about Montana Indigenous Peoples.
Writing
Write multifaceted arguments that support claims and counterclaims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.
Write informative texts that examine and convey advanced ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.
Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective narrative techniques, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

Develop and strengthen writing by planning, organizing, drafting, revising, implementing feedback, and editing to produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
Demonstrate stylistically appropriate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.
Research and Inquiry
Conduct both short and in-depth research projects that answer questions or solve problems, using multiple reliable sources and demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

Gather and synthesize relevant information from multiple sources, using advanced research strategies, citing accurately and appropriately and providing an annotated bibliography according to a standard style.
Conduct research using self-generated questions by analyzing sources for bias and misinformation, including culturally diverse sources and those by and about Montana Indigenous Peoples.
Speaking and Listening
Initiate and engage in a range of collaborative discussions with a variety of partners on topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.
Evaluate the credibility, accuracy, and presentation of multiple sources in a variety of formats and from multiple perspectives.
Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric; consider the cultural backgrounds and lived experiences of the speaker and audience.
Present a clear and distinct argument that addresses opposing perspectives using information, findings, and supporting evidence, in a manner appropriate to purpose, audience, and task.
